data.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
data.authors: Ferniani M; Sambri I; Huynh T; Pennella R; Tufano G; Herz NJ; Rossi B; Iannaccone A; Trepiccione F; Calcagnì A; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Kidney-specific conditional knockout mice: Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO (models of Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex)
data.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. Constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity further accelerates disease on top of mTORC1-driven pathology.
data.abstract_excerpt: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) and Tuberous Sclerosis (TSC) are inherited cancer syndromes associated with kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis and caused by mutations of the folliculin (FLCN) and TSC1/2 genes, respectively. We and others previously showed that Transcription Factors EB (TFEB) and E3 (TFE3) are the main drivers of the kidney phenotypes observed in mouse models of these conditions. These transcription factors are also responsible for the feedback hyperactivation of the mechanistic Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 (mTORC1), a known tumorigenic factor.

extracted_findings.intervention: Kidney-specific Depdc5, RagC and Flcn/RagC conditional knockouts
extracted_findings.target: mTORC1 vs TFEB/TFE3 in kidney cystogenesis
extracted_findings.effect: mTORC1 hyperactivation is a key driver of kidney cysts and tumours; constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity accelerates the pathology.
